title: Integrate the quadratic potential before taking the remainder
source_anchor: Samplinglib original quadratic feature-risk supplement v1, interface5
target_statement: Let W be measurable and H a complete real inner-product space. Let mu and nu be arbitrary measures, feature:W->H Bochner integrable under each, and y in H. Put m=integral feature dmu, n=integral feature dnu and V(q)=2 inner(m-y,feature(q)). Then V is integrable under both measures. With D=integral V dnu-integral V dmu, one has D=2 inner(m-y,n-m), ||n-y||²-||m-y||²-D=||n-m||², and ||m-y||²+D<=||n-y||². The real function t↦||m+t(n-m)-y||² has derivative D at zero. No probability, finite-mass or equal-mass hypothesis is imposed: m and n are unnormalized integrals.
